name: JW Marriott Phu Quoc Emerald Bay Resort & Spa
positioning: Bill Bensley-designed beach resort on Khem Beach, built around the story of a fictional French university
best_for: Travelers who love playful, story-driven design on a calm beach
Families wanting pool villas, a kids club and gentle waters

facts.text: The resort edges the sand and surf of Khem Beach on Phu Quoc.
Khem Beach has gentle waves and clear water, making it family-friendly.
The Dean's Library, home to more than 1,500 books, is now the resort's reception lobby.
Each room is influenced by a fictional academic department within the signature Indochine design.
All accommodations feature a spacious balcony with a sofa bed.
Bathrooms feature double-height windows, dual washbasins, soaking tubs and marble tiles.
The spa offers locally inspired massages, beauty treatments and wellness therapies.
Complimentary activities include kayaking and sunrise yoga.
The Little Explorers Club offers arts and crafts, interactive games and themed workshops for children.
The Department of Chemistry Bar is lab-themed, with glassware and a periodic table on the ceiling.
Guests get complimentary access to the Kiss of the Sea show.
Guests can take a Lamarck University tour of the resort's story and architecture.

highlights.text: Architect Bill Bensley designed the resort around the story of a fictional 19th-century French university.
In the resort's story, classrooms became guest rooms and the old mushroom mycology wharf became Chanterelle Spa.
The Chanterelle Spa's design is inspired by Alice in Wonderland.
The beachfront Sand Pool, Shell Pool and Sun Pool are designed so the pool's edge meets the sandy beach.
The resort has private pool villas with one, three or seven bedrooms.

considerations.text: The resort sits on the southern shore of Phu Quoc, 10 minutes from Sunset Town.
Condé Nast Traveler says Bensley takes the university theme to extremes in the public spaces.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
